nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ and, for each prime $p$ dividing $n$, let $p^{e_p}$ be the largest power of $p$ dividing $n$. Then the Carmichael index of $n$ is $N(n) = \prod_p \bigl(N(n; p^{e_p}) + 1\bigr)$, the product running over the primes $p$ dividing $n$, where $N(n; p^{e_p})$ is the number of units of $\mathbb{Z}/p^{e_p}\mathbb{Z}$ whose multiplicative order divides $\gcd(p - 1, n/p^{e_p} - 1)$.
nodes.title: Product formula for the Carmichael index

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the Carmichael index $N(n)$, the number of integers $a$ with $0 \le a \le n - 1$ and $a^n \equiv a \pmod{n}$, is not equal to $n - 1$.
nodes.title: The Carmichael index of $n$ is never $n - 1$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Carmichael index $N(n)$ is the number of integers $a$ with $0 \le a \le n - 1$ and $a^n \equiv a \pmod{n}$.
nodes.title: Carmichael index
